reviewers.summary:
Reviewer A (facade topology), 005N, read-only review of 5957e3a..HEAD. I ran nothing; every scenario below is a pixel-level fixture to add, not an observed failure.

I found 2 P0, 4 P1, 5 P2 and 3 P3.

**P0**
- **A1:** `backWallOf` accepts any single thin line (or 2–4 step lines) lying between the two returns' cross-sections as a full back wall. It returns the shallowest such hit, so a landing, step or threshold line inside a recessed entrance becomes the "set-back wall". A grid line is added there and its span is shut, which leaves a phantom BUILT room between that line and the real back wall. §23 forbids this.
- **A2:** the per-interval pocket test is order-dependent. It floods once with the evidence from before the loop, but builds each "shut" flood from the decisions already mutated in that loop. Once an earlier sibling interval is shut, its pocket is counted again in every later sibling's pocket. A carport after a pocket-shut hall mouth is therefore closed when the facade is read left-to-right and left open when mirrored, which breaks §22/§31 with a false closure.

**P1**
- **A3:** `RECESS_MAX_DEPTH_M` plus the recess-before-infill role order turns any walled room up to 4.5 m deep into a RECESS_MOUTH unless its wide mouth reads exactly GLAZING or LEAF_AXIS. Affected cases include a store/utility room or small garage with a single-line vehicle door, and a sliding wall drawn with more than 4 lines. The incumbent shut those on infill; now the room is relabelled RECESS.
- **A4:** a RECESS_MOUTH of 3.2 m or less is still shut by `closureOf`'s per-edge lintel rule whenever the grid edge spans both returns' crossing bands with jambs of at least `minJambPx`. Whether the recess "stays open" therefore depends on which face the grid lines sit on and on half-pixel rounding.
- **A5:** `backWallLines` adds the back wall but never the returns. When a return is not a grid line (short return, below 18 % coverage, not wall-to-wall because its foot sits in the gap, no read tick), the recess shares cells with its neighbour. The result is either a phantom-filled recess or a flooded neighbour.
- **A6:** the mouth signature is read on the mean of the bounding pieces' `axisPx`. A separator is a return's cross-section, whose axis is biased inward by a quarter to half a wall. An inner-face line across a middle recess then reads LEAF_AXIS, and a glazed porch's outer line drops out of `inWall`.

**P2**
- WALL_RETURN has no inner-end support check, which §11 requires.
- The 8-candidate slice is taken in drawing order, so it is orientation-dependent.
- A back-wall line runs across the whole plan and creates incumbent wide-gap decisions far from the recess.
- A RECESS_MOUTH skips the pocket test with no check that its back wall actually holds.
- `cornerJoined` also joins a wall that merely starts at the frame's corner.
- The §31 order test does not shuffle grid lines, separator candidates, intervals or bays, so A2 is invisible to it.

**P3**
- `lineAdded` is mislabelled false on the outline-override pass.
- Recess depth and return length are measured from the grid line (often the outer face, set by a chain), not the wall axis.
- `IntervalRole` UNRESOLVED is never emitted, so ambiguity is never named.

findings.title: A single thin line (or 2–4 step lines) between the returns is accepted as the recess back wall, shallowest hit wins: phantom room fills the recess
findings.claim: At every depth, the two returns' cross-sections pass the piece filter: for a crossing wall, readWallLine returns axisPx≈at, so |axisPx−at|≤0.75t always holds. The hole between them (≤ maxHolePx) counts as covered when gapSignature reads GLAZING, LEAF_AXIS or LEAF_FACE. gapStrokes is called without leftEnds/rightEnds and both jambs are non-`along`, so runsPast is false for any line abutting the returns. backWallOf returns the FIRST depth whose cover is at least 0.9. As a result, a landing, step, threshold or floor-finish line across the recess becomes its 'set-back wall'. The docstring's guarantee that 'two returns' cross-sections with the mouth's width of nothing between them are not a wall' is defeated by a single 1-px line. patternAcross is also not applied here, unlike at the mouth.
findings.failureScenario: In compound-facade.test.ts, take entranceAndGarage() and add `p.line(122, 250, 177, 250)` (a landing edge 1.2 m inside the recess). With linePx=280: at d=24, at=256, row 250 is inside the ±9 px band (offset −6, inWall), so the signature is LEAF_FACE and cover is 60/60. The back wall is read at 256, depth 1.2 m. backWallLines adds Y:256 (the nearest existing line, 233.5, is 22.5 px away, more than 9). structuralEvidence shuts Y:256 over [120,180]. Cells x∈[114,186], y∈[233.5,256] are bounded by the lintel-shut real back wall, the two return bands and the new evidence, so they are enclosed and become BUILT. Expect classAt(150,240)==='RECESS'; predicted 'BUILT', and depthM 1.2 instead of 2.0. Two lines (`p.line(120,248,179,248).line(120,256,179,256)`, i.e. steps) read as GLAZING and give the same result.
findings.proposedFix: In backWallOf, count a hole as covered only when at least one of its neighbours is wall ink of the back wall itself (an `along` piece, `inside(l)||inside(r)`). Alternatively, when both neighbours are cross-sections, require the returns' measured inward runs to end within ~1.5t of this depth: the returns turn into the wall there. Also apply patternAcross (as at the mouth) so tread patterns are never infill. Prefer the depth with the most along-wall ink over the shallowest depth that reaches 0.9.

findings.title: Per-interval pocket test is enumeration-order dependent: an earlier sibling's pocket is re-counted in later siblings (orientation-dependent false closure)
findings.claim: `reachedOpen` is flooded once (line 2053) with the evidence from before the loop. `shut` is rebuilt per interval from `collinear.filter(OPENING_IN_WALL)`, which includes intervals mutated to OPENING earlier in the same loop (`g.decision = …`). For any interval after a sibling that the pocket test shut, the pocket therefore contains the sibling's pocket too (reached in base, not in shut). 005N makes sibling intervals on one facade line adjacent in `collinear`, and they are pushed in ascending pixel order, so mirroring changes which sibling inherits the pocket. §16 asks that each atomic interval be tested on its own pocket, and §22/§31 ask for invariance.
findings.failureScenario: Start from house() and clear(120,FRONT,339,279). Add the recess: returnAt 108/150, returnAt 180/100, wallH(108,191,228)+doorH(135,155,228). Add the §16 undrawn mouth 192..251 into a 27 m² hall: returnAt(252,100), wallH(180,263,100)+doorH(200,240,100). Then add a carport 264..339: wallH(264,351,160), returnAt(340,160); it is open only at its mouth, 3.8 m × 4.8 m ≈ 18 m², limit max(6, 2.5·3.8²)=36.1. In 'id' the hall mouth is processed first and shut (27 > 22.5). The carport's pocket then counts hall + carport ≈ 45 m² > 36.1, so the carport becomes OPENING_IN_WALL and builtAt(300,220) is true. In 'mx' the carport goes first (18 m² < 36.1) and stays open. The TRANSFORMS loop must disagree.
findings.proposedFix: Make the pass Jacobi-style. Freeze the OPENING set before the loop (`const before = collinear.filter(OPENING)`) and build each interval's shut flood from `before + g` only. Alternatively, recompute `reachedOpen` per g from the same evidence minus g. Then apply all decisions after the loop. Add a §31 test that permutes `collinear`/interval order (and grid-line and bay order), not only bands, chains and callouts.

findings.title: Any walled room ≤4.5 m deep becomes RECESS_MOUTH unless its mouth reads exactly GLAZING or LEAF_AXIS; the recess branch pre-empts the infill branch
findings.claim: The recess test is purely geometric: returns at both ends plus a back wall within min(returns, 4.5 m) covering 90 %. A room behind a facade opening has exactly that: side walls and a back wall with a door. The role order checks `recess` before `infill >= minInfill && !infillRunsPast && jambInk`. A shallow room whose wide mouth is drawn as one line at a face (LEAF_FACE, i.e. a vehicle/sectional door), with more than 4 lines (DASHED, e.g. a sliding HS wall with sashes), or with a pattern on both sides (patternAcross gives DASHED) is therefore RECESS_MOUTH. The pocket test then skips it, and its OUTSIDE cells are relabelled RECESS. The incumbent's infill rule would have closed it. §14 says the neighbour of a recess is decided independently as OPENING_IN_WALL.
findings.failureScenario: Take entranceAndGarage(), but make the right-hand interval a 3.6 m × 3.3 m utility room instead of a 6.5 m garage: clear 192..263, wallH(180,275,190)+doorH(200,220,190), returnAt(264,190), vehicleDoor(192,263). left = right ≈ 3.9 m and the back wall at axis 195.5 gives depth 4.2 m ≤ 4.5, so recess is set. The mouth line at row 276 is at offset 4 > 3 from axis 272, so it reads LEAF_FACE, which does not shut. Role is RECESS_MOUTH and builtAt(228,240) is false (relabelled RECESS). Expect OPENING_IN_WALL and the room built.
findings.proposedFix: Run the drawn-infill test before the recess test. When infill ≥ minInfill stops at both ink jambs inside the wall band (the same condition as the OPENING_IN_WALL branch), do not label the interval RECESS_MOUTH. If the mouth line is plausibly a step, emit UNRESOLVED and carry both readings rather than choosing open. At minimum, require for RECESS_MOUTH that the back wall carries a door-sized hole or glazing (the entrance) and that the mouth has no infill passing the incumbent rule.

findings.title: RECESS_MOUTH ≤3.2 m is still shut by the per-edge lintel rule in closureOf, depending on grid-line placement and half-pixel rounding
findings.claim: The compound decision for a recess is 'OPEN_SIDE, never shut', but closureOf independently treats a hole ≤ maxOpeningPx between two wall pieces with jambs ≥ minJambPx as shut. wallIntervals counts the returns as crossing bands. Whether the recess mouth edge is shut therefore depends on where the X grid lines sit. Lines on the returns' outer faces (e.g. from chain ticks) give clipped pieces of a full wall, so the edge is shut. Lines on the return axes give pieces of (t−1)/2 vs minJambPx=t/2, which flips with odd/even widths, or when the returns are thicker than the dominant wall. The synthetic tests pass only because their 12 px returns clip to 5.5 px < 6. Most entrance recesses are 1.5–3 m wide, so they are inside the lintel convention.
findings.failureScenario: Run entranceAndGarage() with an extra read chain whose ticks sit on the returns' outer faces, e.g. chain('cz','HORIZONTAL',[40,108,192,360]), so grid lines land at X:108 and X:192. The facade edge [108,192] has pieces [108,120] and [180,192] (jambs 12 ≥ 6) and a hole of 60 ≤ 64 px, so it is shut. The recess cell is then enclosed by the back-wall line and the returns and becomes BUILT. Expect classAt(150,255)==='RECESS'; predicted 'BUILT'. The same happens without a chain if the returns are drawn 16 px thick while the dominant wall stays 12 px.
findings.proposedFix: Pass the RECESS_MOUTH intervals into edgesFor/closureOf as 'held-open' stretches on their facade line. Holes overlapping them are not added by the lintel rule, and their wall/line share is not counted toward closure. This is symmetric to how `structural` evidence is injected. Add the chain-on-faces and thick-return variants to the §21 fixtures.

findings.title: Body closure needs grid lines at the recess returns, but only the back wall is ever added
findings.claim: `backWallLines` adds the set-back wall line, but nothing adds perpendicular lines at the separator return or at the jamb return. A recess return is not wall-to-wall in `spansWallToWall`: its foot sits in the facade gap, so it lands on no facade band. Its band coverage is about depth/plan size: a 1.5 m return in a 10 m plan is 0.15 < minBandCoverage 0.18. If no read chain ticks there (unread segments are dropped), the return has no grid line, and the recess shares cells with the room or garage beside it. Two outcomes follow. If the facade edge closure is ≥ 0.62 (the mouth is a small part of a long edge), the recess fills as BUILT (phantom). Otherwise the back-wall evidence covers only [from,to] of a longer edge, the edge stays open, and the neighbour floods through the 'open recess mouth'. The recess relabel only touches OUTSIDE cells and cannot repair either. §13/§17 require the recess to remain RECESS and the body to close.
findings.failureScenario: Use house() with a 16 m living-room front: glazeFront(60,107), a recess 120..179 with returnAt(108,240) and returnAt(180,240) (1.4 m, coverage ≈ 0.16, no tick), wallH(108,191,240)+doorH(135,155,240), and glazeFront(192,299). X lines exist only at 40/359. The facade edge [40,359] is about 0.8 covered, so it is shut, and the cell row facade..Y:245.5 is BUILT across the recess. Expect classAt(150,260)==='RECESS'; predicted BUILT.
findings.proposedFix: In backWallLines, also add an X/Y grid line at each recess interval's bounding returns: the separator piece's axis, and the jamb return's probe position. Do this only when no line lies within min(minCell, t), with the same `why`/support provenance as the back-wall line, and add those keys to `setBack` so the facade reader skips them.

findings.title: Mouth signature axis is biased inward when an end is a separator (a cross-section): middle recesses misread LEAF_AXIS or lose glazing lines
findings.claim: For a wall crossing the facade line, readWallLine's axisPx is the midpoint of the qualifying run, clipped by the cross window. Because the return extends only inward, that midpoint is ~t/4–t/2 inward of the facade axis (synthetic: 270.5 or 267.5 vs 273.5). `axisPx = (lp.axisPx + rp.axisPx)/2` then shifts the gapStrokes band and the LEAF_AXIS window (±0.25t). For an interval bounded by two separators (a recess between a garage and a living room, the common central-entrance layout), a line on the facade's inner face reads LEAF_AXIS. The recess is then 'shut' as an enclosed porch (OPENING_IN_WALL, so BUILT). Also, the outer glazing line of a genuinely glazed porch can fall outside `inWall` (|c−axis| > t/2+1), so GLAZING degrades to LEAF_FACE and the porch reads RECESS. gapStrokes' own halfOf already notes that a crossing wall's geometry must not stand in for the line's.
findings.failureScenario: Draw [glazeFront 60..107 | returnAt(108,150) | recess 120..179 with wallH(108,191,228)+doorH | returnAt(180,150) | glazeFront 192..299], so the recess is bounded by two separators, and add `p.line(120,268,179,268)` (a threshold line on the inner face). Both separators' axisPx ≈ 270.5, so centre is 271, offset −3 and the line reads LEAF_AXIS with width 3 m ≤ 3.2. The role is OPENING_IN_WALL ('an enclosed porch') and the recess cells become BUILT. Expect RECESS_MOUTH. Mirror case: glazing at rows 276/271 between two separators with the facade band axis as linePx loses row 276 from inWall, giving LEAF_FACE.
findings.proposedFix: Take the mouth axis only from `along` pieces (the facade's own stretches). If neither end is along, use the facade band's axis: the parent jambs' band window centre ((bandLo+bandHi)/2), not `parent.linePx`, which may be a chain face line. Pass the cross-section pieces to gapStrokes only for halfOf/past.

findings.title: WALL_RETURN accepted on inward length alone: no check that it joins a back wall or structural side (§11 'source support at relevant ends')
findings.claim: separatorOf accepts WALL_RETURN whenever the longest perpendicular wall-thick run touching the facade reaches max(0.9 m, 3t). This is checked before the POST/WALL test, so a free-standing block ≥3t deep (a chimney/storage block, a planter or wing fin, an outdoor-kitchen wall standing in a carport mouth) is a return. Its inner end is never checked for a junction with a back wall or another wall. returnRun also accepts perpendicular ink anywhere within ±1.5t of the probe and up to t behind the facade without being connected to the piece. A false separator splits an open carport/porch into intervals, which then feed A2's cascade and per-interval limits.
findings.failureScenario: Draw entranceAndCarport() plus a 0.6 × 1.8 m solid block on the facade line in the middle of the carport mouth (p.wall(296,232,307,279)), standing free with nothing at its inner end. It is accepted as WALL_RETURN and the carport becomes two 1.6 m intervals. Each is ≤ maxOpening, so closureOf's lintel rule can shut them between the block's crossing band and the jambs, and the carport is BUILT.
findings.proposedFix: Require the return run's inner end to meet a wall: at the run's far end, readWallLine across it must find a perpendicular wall-thick piece (a T/L), or the run must reach the back wall found for the adjacent interval. Otherwise mark it NOT_A_SEPARATOR ('a fin, no wall relation'). Read the probe with a narrower cross window (±0.5t) so adjacent unrelated ink is not borrowed.

findings.title: Separator bound slices the first 8 pieces in drawing order: mirror-dependent separator set
findings.claim: `inside.slice(0, COMPOUND_BOUNDS.separators)` keeps the 8 leftmost/topmost candidates. On a gap with more than 8 wall-thick pieces (a colonnade of posts, a pergola on the facade line, a glazed front with thick piers), a real return in position 9+ is dropped in one orientation and kept in the mirrored one. §22 requires an invariant semantic result. `spans.length < COMPOUND_BOUNDS.spans` (plan-decomposition.ts:1487) has the same issue across axes under rotation.
findings.failureScenario: Draw a 10 m facade gap with 8 POST blocks at 1 m spacing from the left and a WALL_RETURN near the right end. In 'id' the return is never judged and the span returns null (incumbent). In 'mx' it is the first candidate and splits the span.
findings.proposedFix: When inside.length exceeds the bound, return null (record 'too many candidates: incumbent reading') instead of slicing. Alternatively, filter POST-kind pieces first (they can never be separators unless they have a return) and then refuse if more than the bound remain. Do the same for the span bound: refuse to read any span when the count exceeds the bound, rather than taking the first N.

findings.title: RECESS_MOUTH bypasses the pocket test with no check that its back wall actually holds in the grid
findings.claim: A RECESS_MOUTH records pocketM2 and stays open unconditionally. Before 005N, an interior behind a gap larger than max(6, 2.5w²) shut that gap. If the back-wall closure does not take in the grid (A5's missing return lines, the evidence covering only [from,to] of a longer edge, a snapped line, or the override pass), the whole interior floods through an 'open recess mouth' and the safety net is gone. §13 says the back wall must block outside flood into the building interior; nothing verifies that it does.
findings.failureScenario: In A5's geometry, make the facade edge's closure fall below 0.62 (the recess mouth is a large share of the edge). The back-line edge is open beside the recess, so the hall and the rooms flood: pocketM2 ≫ width×depth of the recess, yet the decision stays OPEN_SIDE and the interior becomes OUTSIDE.
findings.proposedFix: For RECESS_MOUTH, compare pocketM2 with the recess rectangle (widthM × depthM × (1+slack)). If it is larger, the back wall did not close in this grid. Fall through to the incumbent pocket rule, or mark the interval UNRESOLVED with a 'back wall does not hold' reason; never leave the mouth open silently.

findings.title: Added back-wall line spans the whole plan and creates incumbent wide-gap decisions far from the recess
findings.claim: The second collinearWideGaps pass runs the incumbent reader on the new line everywhere: `setBack` only stops the compound reader. Any two along bands lying on that y elsewhere produce new COLLINEAR_GAP decisions, OPENING by any infill line in the band window, or by the pocket rule or shutPocketMouths. They can shut edges across a carport or terrace at that depth, and they enter H1's evidence and `evidencedCount`. The line also cuts every room it crosses into thinner cells. backWallLineOf's reach of min(minCell, depth/2) means a shallow recess (depth < 0.9 m) can add a line closer than minCell to an existing one, which thinLines would never allow.
findings.failureScenario: Draw a recess with a back wall at depth 2 m beside a carport whose rear storage room has a wall band on the same y beyond the carport. The new line yields a gap across the carport between the back-wall band and that band. With a drawn kerb or edge line on that y it is shut by infill, or in the shutPocketMouths reading by its pocket, and the carport's rear half becomes BUILT.
findings.proposedFix: Give added lines a span limit (probe only within the recess's [from−t, to+t]), or exclude setBack lines from collinearWideGaps entirely. Their only job is to carry the structural evidence and the cell cut. Enforce |added − existing| ≥ minCell or snap.

findings.title: cornerJoined also joins a wall that merely starts at the frame's corner (collinear continuation or wing), growing the extent
findings.claim: The test is: a frame band c ends within 1.5t of b's axis, and c's axis lies in b's run (±1.5t). For a long wall-thick band b that continues the house's side wall from its corner outward (a retaining or driveway wall, a wing wall or garden wall drawn wall-thick and separated by a break), c (the front wall) ends on b's axis and b's run starts at c's axis, so it is 'joined'. The extent grows to b's far end. The orchestrator reports murajach's ground registration moving from ~1.55 to 2.451 cm/px after this change. plan-resolution.ts:574 feeds planExtent into the CHAIN_RECT readings under every lattice scale, so the extent change can alter which scale wins. That should be traced to the band that was joined.
findings.failureScenario: In the §21.22 extentOf harness, use the detached case and add a 0.6 m-thick band from the house's bottom-right corner running down 8 m (x 348..359, y 280+gap..440, separated by a 2 px break). It is joined and extent.y1 is about 440. Expect it not joined.
findings.proposedFix: Require b to be the far wall of a closed structure: b must have a second frame-reaching or joined band ending on it (two walls from the frame meet b, which makes a garage), or b must be parallel-offset from the frame's own side wall by more than 1.5t (not collinear with it). Record which band was joined in `why` and in the digest so the murajach drift can be checked against it.

findings.title: §31 order test omits the required grid-line, separator, interval and bay enumeration shuffles
findings.claim: The brief §31 lists wall bands, grid lines, separator candidates, callouts, intervals and bays. The test shuffles only bands, chains and callouts, and its header claims that intervals are 'never from an enumeration'. They are consumed in enumeration order by the pocket loop (A2), and separators by the bounded slice (A8). The scene also has a single non-recess OPEN_SIDE interval, so no cascade can show up.
findings.failureScenario: A2's fixture passes the existing order test unchanged, because the test never permutes `collinear` or interval order.
findings.proposedFix: Add a test seam: an internal option that reverses or permutes collinearWideGaps output, interval order and bay order. Assert byte-identical decisions on a scene with ≥2 non-recess OPEN_SIDE siblings (A2's fixture), plus the mirror of every §21 family with more than one separator.

findings.title: Recess depth and return length measured from the grid line (often the outer face), not the wall axis
findings.claim: depthM = |back.px − parent.linePx| and inwardOf uses parent.linePx. When the facade grid line is a chain line on the outer face (as in the synthetic plans, 280 vs axis 273.5), depth and returnM are inflated by about t/2 (0.2–0.3 m). That shifts the RECESS_MAX_DEPTH_M and RETURN_MIN_M cut-offs, and the 3t guard, against the stated semantics.
findings.failureScenario: A 4.3 m-deep garage-like pocket measured from an outer-face chain line reads 4.55 m and escapes the recess path, while the same plan with the line on the axis reads it as a recess.
findings.proposedFix: Measure from the facade wall's axis (the jambs' band centre, (bandLo+bandHi)/2) rather than linePx.

findings.title: Diagnostics: lineAdded false on the override pass; UNRESOLVED role never emitted
findings.claim: On the outline-override pass, `setBack` is empty (lines are only added when `!override`), so `interval.recess.lineAdded` is recorded false even though the line was added by the first pass and inherited through override.linesY. The Evidence Pack then misreports the linkage. `IntervalRole` declares UNRESOLVED (§12), but no branch emits it, so ambiguous mouths (a step line vs a door; A3, A6) are resolved by preference instead of being named.
findings.failureScenario: Any plan accepted by boundaryExtension with a recess: the 12c-compound-facades.json from the final decomposition shows lineAdded:false for a line that exists only because of backWallLines.
findings.proposedFix: Mark added lines in their GridLine (e.g. support.kind or a why prefix) and derive lineAdded from the line, not from the per-call set. Emit UNRESOLVED where two branches' conditions both hold (A3).

I traced the code end to end and could not refute the mechanism. I ran nothing (read-only).

Code path (packages/reconstruction/src/compound-facade.ts, 250-283):
- Setup: t=12, the line runs along rows (axis 'Y'), inward=-1, interval from=120 to=180. Both returns (x 108..191, rows 150..279) are 123.5+ px long, so reach=min(·,90)+12 and deepest=90. maxOpeningM defaults to 3.2 (plan-decomposition.ts:371), so maxHolePx=64 and the 60 px hole passes the line-269 check.
- At each depth, readWallLine (boundary-evidence.ts:304) reads every window across a return as ink, so the run's midpoint gives axisPx=round(at). For linePx=280, d=24: at=256, the return pieces are 108–120 and 180–192, their axisPx is 256, and along=false (12 < 15). They pass the filter at line 265: |0|≤9 and |256−280|≥15. Nothing between them is solid.
- gapStrokes(centre=256, band=round(max(9, 6+2))=9, rows 247..265) sees the added row-250 line with coverage 56/60=0.93, runs=1, and inWall (|250−256|=6 ≤ half+1=7).
- runsPast cannot fire. The `separate` test needs |c−axisPx|>7 and fails. Even at offsets 8–9 it fails, because the return's own ink fills both sampled rows. `ends` is false because leftEnds/rightEnds are not passed. So a cross-section jamb can never flag runs-past, even for a line that carries on past the returns.
- gapSignature gives LEAF_FACE (offset −6 > 3). The hole counts as covered, cover=60/60, and the shallowest depth wins: back wall px=256, depth 1.2 m. For linePx=273.5 the same thing happens at d=18 (at=255.5, centre 256, depth 0.875 m). patternAcross is not applied here, so treads (2–4 lines) give GLAZING with the same result.
- The mouth is BLANK, so the role is RECESS_MOUTH. backWallLines adds Y:256, because no existing line is within min(minCell, 12) px. structuralEvidence then shuts Y:256 over [120,180]. The cells between Y:256 and the real back wall (or the hall line) are closed on all sides: the returns, the lintel-convention back wall, and the new evidence. They become enclosed and BUILT.

Nothing guards this. architecture.md §6 does not list it as a limit, and its line 31 claims that "two returns' cross-sections are never a back wall", which this path contradicts. The only related test (compound-facade.test.ts:184) uses diagonal hatching, which never reaches 0.7 row coverage.

Fixture that would confirm it (compound-facade.test.ts):

A loggia or recess whose back is a 3.5-6 m glazed screen (common in modern houses) gets no recess. The interval goes OPEN_SIDE with no back-wall grid line, so the loggia cell merges with the room behind. The pocket test then sees loggia plus room and shuts the mouth, and the loggia becomes BUILT (§23 'no phantom room fills recess'). The loggia fixture (family 9) uses a 2.6 m glazed back.
findings.failureScenario: Family 9 fixture with the recess widened to 4 m (returns at 108 and 200, mouth 120..199) and the back wall fully glazed: p.clear(120,228,199,239) plus two lines at y 231 and 236. findings.title: runsPast row tie-break is orientation-dependent
findings.claim: The best row is the first row scanning bandLo to bandHi upward with the strictly longest stroke. Two glazing lines of equal length tie, and the inner line wins in 'id' while the outer line wins under mirrorY/turn. carries() then checks only best.row +/- 1. If one line of the pair continues past the jamb and the other does not (a plinth or sill line on the outer face beyond a short pier or a corner), runsPast and the role flip with orientation. The TRANSFORMS fixtures never have unequal carry-on on tied rows.
findings.failureScenario: Family 4 (recess + glazed window). Make the window's right jamb the building corner within 2 m: p.clear(348, FRONT, 359, 279) style, with the outer glazing line (FRONT+8) extended 30 px past the corner and the inner one not. 'id' checks FRONT+3 (no carry) and gives OPENING_IN_WALL. 'mirrorY' checks the outer line (carries) and gives OPEN_SIDE.
findings.proposedFix: Evaluate carries() for every row whose stroke reaches the interval's infill threshold and combine them with an orientation-free rule (for example, runs past only if the majority of qualifying rows carry on). Or reuse gapStrokes' per-stroke runsPast, which is computed per drawn line.

findings.title: No fixture varies scale, anisotropy, wall thickness or grid reference; several families run in one orientation only
findings.claim: Every 005N fixture is 5 cm/px, mppX = mppY (plan.ts registration), 12 px walls equal to the sheet wall, and chains on the outer faces. Several thresholds scale with the sheet wall in pixels (POST bbox 2.5t, along 1.25t, RETURN 3t, back-wall step t/2, envelope reach 1.5t), so the invariance claims rest on one scale. Families 6, 13, 16, 'post in a mouth', bays 10-12, the §21.22 extent test and all §23 end-to-end tests are id-only. §22 asks for major fixtures normal, mirrored and rotated.
findings.failureScenario: Not covered: entranceAndGarage at 2 cm/px with 30 px exterior and 12 px sheet walls; the same raster stretched 1.25x in y with metresPerPixelY = 0.04; chains on the inner faces; the attached-garage extent on the -x and +-y sides.
findings.proposedFix: Parameterize PlanDrawing by cm/px, wall px and a per-axis stretch, and the chain ticks by face (outer, axis, inner). Run the major families across that grid times TRANSFORMS, and run the §21.22 extent and §23 e2e tests at least under mirrorX and turn90.

findings.title: Facade context only on the bounding-rect envelope sides, so compound spans on L/T/U plans' inner facades are never read
findings.claim: inward is set only when the gap's line lies within 1.5 sheet walls of the walled envelope's rect side. In any non-rectangular plan, the facade of the set-back wing (where an entrance and garage door commonly share a line) is not an envelope side and falls back to the merged incumbent reading. The note states this limit for murajach. It conflicts with §5's 'generic facade-local' path: the rule depends on which facade happens to be extreme. The 1.5t reach also uses the sheet wall, so an inner-face grid line of a 2x-thick exterior wall is out of reach.
findings.failureScenario: An L-shaped house: main body 40..359 x 40..279 with a wing projecting to y 359 on x 40..139. The entrance recess plus separator plus garage door of entranceAndGarage sit on the main front line y 268..279 (x 150..300), which is no longer the envelope's bottom side (now y 359). The reader returns null and the gap is weighed as one, the pre-005N failure.
findings.proposedFix: Derive the facade side from topology instead of the rect. For example, the line is a facade where the strict H0 flood reaches the cells on exactly one side along the gap, with inward pointing to the unreached side. Or use the boundary outline's edges when present. Use the jamb's measured thickness, not the sheet wall, for the reach.

findings.title: Two accepted separators can leave a sub-MIN_INTERVAL interval between them
findings.claim: The MIN_INTERVAL_M check compares a candidate only with the span's two ends, never with the previous accepted separator. Two returns (or a return and a pier split by a break wider than t/2) a few pixels apart create a 'mouth' narrower than 0.6 m. It gets its own role, decision, pocket test and evidence entry.
findings.failureScenario: Two 12 px returns at x 180 and 200 inside a facade gap give an 8 px (0.4 m) interval at 192..200 with role OPEN_SIDE, pocket-tested on its own.
findings.proposedFix: When cutting, merge consecutive accepted separators whose gap is below max(MIN_INTERVAL_M/mpp, t) into one separator, and record why.

findings.title: backWallReads = 64 with step t/2 caps the search short of 4.5 m on thin-wall sheets
findings.claim: The number of reads needed is about (4.5 m/(t*mpp) - 1.5)*2 = 9/wall_m - 3. When the sheet wall is about 0.13 m or less (sheets whose modal band is a 12 cm partition), 64 reads reach only about 33.5t, roughly 4.0 m. A recess 4.0-4.5 m deep is then missed for scale reasons alone.
findings.failureScenario: entranceAndGarage at 3 cm/px with a 4 px sheet wall and the recess back wall at 4.3 m. The loop stops at about 4.0 m, so there is no recess.
findings.proposedFix: Use step = max(1, round(t/2), ceil((deepest - 1.5t)/COMPOUND_BOUNDS.backWallReads)) so the bound limits work, not depth.

findings.title: backWallLineOf can choose a grid line between the mouth and the back wall
findings.claim: The docstring says 'never one nearer the mouth', but the filter is |l.px - backWallPx| <= min(minCellPx, depth/2) on either side. structuralEvidence then shuts that line across the interval, and the recess relabel stops at it. A strip of up to 0.45 m between the chosen line and the real back wall is enclosed and can read BUILT inside the recess.
findings.failureScenario: A recess 1.4 m deep with an existing chain-tick grid line 0.4 m in front of its back wall. The line is chosen, a 0.4 m strip in the recess is shut on all sides, and the cell is BUILT.
findings.proposedFix: Only accept lines with (l.px - backWallPx)*inward >= -t/2 (at or behind the wall's axis). Otherwise add the back-wall line.

findings.title: cornerJoined: the join is carried by any frame band's end, however far it runs, and is tested in one orientation
findings.claim: The join is symmetric and only adds the joined band's axis, which lies within 1.5 walls of a frame band's end, so its growth is bounded by that frame band's run. That run is not itself bounded to the building: a wall-thick garden or retaining wall continuing collinearly from the house wall carries the join to a perpendicular wall at its far end. The extent test (§21.22) only places the garage at +x.
findings.failureScenario: In the weak branch, the house's front wall band continues as one ink run 8 m beyond the corner, as a garden wall ending on a perpendicular wall-thick fence. The fence is joined and the extent grows 8 m. Not tested: attached garage at -x, -y, +y.
findings.proposedFix: Require the frame band c to be a wall of the building at its end, for example its run beyond the near rect is no longer than the joined band b's run (a corner of a mass, not a garden wall). Run test 22 under mirrorX and turn90.

findings.title: HEAD runs the compound reader on unit-placeholder (unscaled) plans: decisions change and a full-sheet solid layer is built that the incumbent never built
findings.claim: At HEAD, `facadeCompoundReader` is created for every decomposition with an envelope, including placeholderRegistration plans (layout.ts:553, mpp = 1 m/px, confidence 0). decomposePlan skips boundaryExtension for confidence <= 0 (line ~1803), so before 005N no solidLayer was built for these plans. Now contextOf() builds one: erode/dilate plus CCL, with two W·H Int32Array buffers and the labels array kept in the WeakMap while the sheet mask lives. Every gap > maxOpeningM/1 = 3.2 px with jambs on an envelope side reaches compoundSpanOf, including gaps > 8 px that the incumbent skipped outright. Thresholds become degenerate in px: minMouth = t, RETURN_MIN = 3t, recess depth 4.5 px. A FACADE_PIER (WALL part, along ≥ 1.25t) can still be accepted; its intervals get widthM = pixels-as-metres (> 8 → OPEN_SIDE) and its ink enters H1 shut evidence via structuralEvidence. That changes evidencedCount, H1 closures and the scores of upper-storey plans that 005L registration matches on. This is also the most likely cause of the measured >15% regression that §32 requires explaining: the ABAB rerun (HEAD, no alias) shows D01 409→779/402→876 ms read, D03 930→1787/911→1852, D05 462→909/475→896, galaktyka 861→1478/728→1521, aster-viii 138→254/153→285. These are rows whose packages have plan frames with no PLAN_XZ registration (D01: 3 frames, 1 registration; galaktyka 3/1; aster 2/1; D03 14/2; D05 3/1). On the phone (nodejs-mobile), each such plan adds a transient ~8·W·H bytes and retains 4·W·H.
findings.failureScenario: Package with a dimensioned ground plan and an undimensioned first-floor plan, i.e. placeholder registration. First floor: a 3000×2000 px mask whose front wall has two 30 px windows separated by an 18 px wall stretch (12 px walls) that an interior partition joins. The incumbent skips the 78 px gap (> 8 px) and builds no solid layer. HEAD builds a 6M px solid layer (~48 MB of Int32 for labels+stack), accepts the stretch as FACADE_PIER and emits two OPEN_SIDE intervals of widthM 30. The pier ink is added as shut evidence on that line, so H1 edges on the first-floor plan change before 005L storey registration reads them.
findings.proposedFix: Commit the worktree gate (`registration.confidence > 0 ? facadeCompoundReader(...) : undefined`). Strengthen its test: assert byte-identical `cells`, `wideOpenings` and `hypotheses` of the unscaled decomposition against a golden snapshot made at 5957e3a, not just `compoundFacades === undefined`. Then rerun ABAB and the 42-row matrix at the committed SHA, since both were measured without the gate. Confirm with a vite alias that counts solidLayer and compoundSpanOf calls per row split by registration.confidence; the D0x rows should drop to the 5957e3a counts.

findings.title: No multi-storey end-to-end fixture with a compound front (§23 '005L per-storey geometry remains correct', §28 synthetic garage-with-one-storey-wing)
findings.claim: Every 005N end-to-end fixture compiles a single GROUND frame (`graphOf([frame])`). No storey test (storey-support, storey-council, storey-emission) contains a facade gap with an accepted separator, so the interaction between 005N output and 005L is never exercised. That output is RECESS cells, back-wall grid lines added to incumbent.linesX (which boundaryExtension and the resolver reuse), and the garage now inside the body. The interaction is real: storeySupportOf clips an upper region to the masses below and marks the uncarried part as overhang. Today the emitter residual keeps the recess inside the rectangular mass, which masks it. Any change there turns an upper floor over a recessed entrance (a common podcień) into BEYOND_TOLERANCE or a clipped region. The dev-matrix storey rows (A06, A07, zurawkach, tunbergiach, Marcówki) produced no span, so they do not cover it either.
findings.failureScenario: A ground plan like `entranceAndGarage(true)` (5 cm/px, 12 px walls, recess between returns at x 108 and 180, garage 192–251), plus a FIRST_FLOOR frame covering only x 40–263 (the house and the recess, not the garage), with its own chains. Expected: house two storeys, garage one storey, upper floor carried over the recess (overhang NONE or WITHIN_TOLERANCE), recess still RECESS on the ground. Nothing currently asserts any of this.
findings.proposedFix: Add a §23/§28 fixture in compound-facade-emission.test.ts compiling two frames (ground with the compound front; first floor over house + recess; garage one storey). Assert storeys per mass, the upper region's overhang, the storeys digest relations, and that the ground compound span and roles equal the single-storey run.

findings.title: backWallLines lets an added line suppress later recesses in enumeration order: the grid, and with it the recess/built split, differs under mirroring
findings.claim: `existing` includes lines added for earlier recess intervals, and intervals are visited left→right along the line (spans by line px). Take two recess intervals whose back walls lie within `reach = min(minCellPx, depth/2)` of each other with no original grid line at either: the first one visited gets the line and the second reuses it. A mirror reverses the visiting order, so the line lands on the other back wall. structuralEvidence then shuts the other interval's span on that line, and the RECESS relabel uses `gridLinePx`. The result: one recess is shortened by the offset while the room strip behind the other is lost. §22 requires a mirror-invariant semantic result.
findings.failureScenario: Scene at 5 cm/px, WALL 12 (minCellPx 9), house ring 40..359×40..279, front clears (70..159, 268..279) and (172..279, 268..279). Returns at x 58, 160 and 280 running up to y≈186. Back wall A: wallH(58..171, y 194) with axis ≈ 199.5. Back wall B: wallH(160..291, y 186) with axis ≈ 191.5. Chains only on the overall dimensions, so no grid line exists at either back wall. runScene(s,'id') puts the added line at ≈199.5; runScene(s,'mirrorX') puts it at ≈191.5 (mirrored back). The two cell sets differ, so built and RECESS areas differ by ≈ 8 px × (wA + wB) ≈ 1.9 m².
findings.proposedFix: Make the choice orientation-free. Either decide each interval only against the ORIGINAL lines and add a line for every back wall without an original line within reach (never let added lines suppress each other). Or collect all candidates first and visit them in a mirror-invariant order, e.g. by (depthM desc, cover desc, widthM desc). Add the two-recess scene above to the TRANSFORMS loop in compound-facade.test.ts.

findings.title: Separator bound truncates by position (`inside.slice(0, 8)`), so which separators are read depends on orientation
findings.claim: `inside` is sorted by `from` and the first 8 pieces are judged. Any ninth or later piece is ignored, and the last interval spans across it. Mirroring reverses which 8 are kept, so separators, intervals and roles differ between a plan and its mirror. That breaks §22 and the 'same source → same segmentation' rule of §31. The spans bound has the same problem at line 1487: X lines then Y lines, by px.
findings.failureScenario: A 14 m front gap holding 10 wall-thick piers, each 18 px and joined to an interior wall (a colonnade or a run of piers between glazed bays). Identity reads piers 1–8 and leaves 9–10 inside one long last interval, which may be > 8 m and so OPEN_SIDE. mirrorX reads piers 3–10 and leaves the long interval at the other end. The roles and pocket tests differ.
findings.proposedFix: When `inside.length > COMPOUND_BOUNDS.separators` (or spans would exceed 24), return null: leave the incumbent reading and record a 'too many separator candidates' note. Never judge a positional prefix. Add a 9+ pier fixture to the mirror test.

findings.title: The '40/42 identical' regression claim compares only modelHash or failure code; for the 20 FAILED rows and non-selected storey plans, digest changes are invisible
findings.claim: dev-matrix-run2.json rows carry outcome, modelHash, code, storeys and footprint only. dom-w-murajach shows `modelChanged: false` although its ground registration and extent changed after cornerJoined, as the task brief itself states. So 'byte-identical when no separator is accepted' is demonstrated only for COMPLETED rows' final models. It is not shown for the plan digest, for failing rows, or for unselected copies, which is where E1 and E6 would show.
findings.failureScenario: A failing row whose upper-storey or alternate plan gained a FACADE_PIER span at HEAD (E1), or whose weak extent widened (E6). The failure code is unchanged, so the matrix reports 'identical'.
findings.proposedFix: Per row, also hash the planDiagnostics digest (minus compoundFacades) and run evidence-pack firstDivergence old vs new. Require identity except on rows with a compound span or an extent 'running into' note, and list those rows explicitly in the report.

findings.title: cornerJoined changes the extent of every weak-frame plan (all storeys, every resolver scale and extent hypothesis) regardless of any facade evidence, and is untested outside one ground fixture
findings.claim: This is the stage's only non-facade behaviour change. It applies whenever held < loose, on any storey, scaled or not, and inside plan-resolution's CHAIN_RECT hypothesis (plan-resolution.ts:574). It widens the frame to the axis of any wall-thick long band at whose axis a frame band's run ends, with no requirement that the joined band encloses anything. On murajach it already moved the metric registration (2.451 vs ~1.55 cm/px). The only tests are the §21.22 attached-vs-detached garage pair on a ground plan.
findings.failureScenario: Weak-frame ground plan (chains describe a detail). The house's south wall band runs on past the house corner as a wall-thick garden wall to x=470 and stops on a wall-thick retaining wall at x≈470 running y 200..330, beyond the 35 % margin. cornerJoined joins the retaining wall and the extent widens to x≈476. More bands become `inside`, the envelope and its facade sides change, and the grid gains cells over the garden. Same on an attic plan whose chains are partial, where a ≥0.7-wall parapet stands at the end of a long wall.
findings.proposedFix: Require the joined band to close a frame: its run must also meet a second frame band's end, or the joined part must have a return back toward the frame. Otherwise record it in the extent `why` without widening. At minimum, add the garden or retaining-wall fixture and an upper-storey weak-frame fixture asserting an unchanged extent and no BUILT cell beyond the house.

findings.title: Redundant work: the back-wall second pass re-reads every compound span, and separatorOf reads returns before rejecting jamb-adjacent ink
findings.claim: alongWallPieces for an existing line does not depend on other lines, so the second `collinearWideGaps` recomputes identical compoundSpanOf results, including up to 64 back-wall reads per interval, plus every incumbent infillAcross. The outline pass and each resolver (extent × scale) decomposition repeat the facade reading again. In compound-facade.ts:222 the three perpendicular returnRun reads run before the minMouth rejection at line 225. The bound naming also misleads: `spans: 24` counts only accepted spans, and `backWallReads: 64` is per interval, giving a worst case ≈ 24·9·64 readWallLine per decomposition.
findings.failureScenario: A plan with a recess whose back wall gets an added line runs the facade reader twice in the incumbent pass and again in the outline pass. A gap with 8 posts near the jambs costs 24 perpendicular reads for pieces rejected on position alone.
findings.proposedFix: Memoize compoundOf inside facadeCompoundReader by `${axis}:${linePx}:${fromPx}:${toPx}:${bandLo}:${bandHi}`, and re-run collinearWideGaps only on the added lines, merging in line order. Move the mouth check before the returnRun probes. Add a per-decomposition readWallLine budget; when it is exhausted, fall back to the incumbent with a recorded note.

findings.title: H1 diagnostics count separators and back walls as 'wide openings closed'
findings.claim: evidencedCount now includes the structural entries (evidenceMap seeds them), so `closedOpenings` and the H1 `why` ('N wide openings closed') count pier ink and recess back walls as openings. Structural evidence alone also switches H1 on (evidencedCount > 0) and enters min(evidenceScores). Non-compound plans are unaffected, but the digest and Evidence Pack misreport compound ones.
findings.failureScenario: A compound span with one FACADE_PIER and two OPEN_SIDE intervals: hypotheses[H1].closedOpenings = 1 and the why says '1 wide opening closed' although no opening was closed.
findings.proposedFix: Count structural entries separately (e.g. `structuralClosures`) and keep closedOpenings for openings only.

findings.title: 12c is emitted for every run, so a pre-005N run record reads as 'read, no spans'; the extent join is not in 12c
findings.claim: `spans: f.compoundFacades ?? []` gives the same 12c for a digest that never ran the reader as for one that found nothing. The `compound-facade` version reaches the run record only through the dev script second-house.ts. The production analysis-service records just service and solver versions, both unchanged although answers changed (A05 now PASS). §19 asks for the 'final body/extent effect'; the cornerJoined bands appear only as a sentence in the extent why. Inserting COMPOUND_FACADES also shifts downstreamOf('EXTENT').
findings.failureScenario: Building a 1.4.0 pack from a 005M run record gives a 12c with empty spans, which a reviewer cannot tell apart from a 005N run with no separators.
findings.proposedFix: Write `compoundFacadeVersion` (or `read: true/false` per copy) into 12c from the digest. Add the joined band ids and corners to the extent record. Consider adding compound-facade and plan-extent to the production run-record versions.

findings.title: Order-invariance test omits the grid-line and bay enumeration shuffles required by §31
findings.claim: Only bands, chains and callouts are shuffled. Grid lines, bays and intervals have no injection point, and nothing asserts invariance under mirror for multi-recess or many-separator scenes, where E3 and E4 are order-sensitive.

findings.proposedFix: Add the E3 and E4 scenes to the TRANSFORMS loop. Where shuffling an internal list is impossible, state that and test the mirror instead.
